texts.screens.granted_because_this_role_name_m: Granted because this role name matches the username; remove the role to remove this automatic assignment.

texts.screens.added_or_removed_in_the_template: Added or removed in the template since the copy, or changed values.
texts.screens.the_package_role_and_commit_this: The package role and commit this role was copied from.
texts.screens.audited_successes_and_failed_che: Audited successes and failed checks older than this are removed every night.
texts.screens.attribute_values_given_with_this: Attribute values given with this assignment.
texts.screens.every_new_user_receives_these_ro: Every new user receives these roles. Existing users keep their roles.
texts.auth.a_declared_authorization_attribute_: A declared authorization attribute, such as `dlis.einvoice.channel`. Its values come from each role assignment.
texts.auth.a_unique_case_sensitive_role_name_a: A unique, case-sensitive role name. A role matching a username is automatically assigned to that user.
texts.auth.the_authorization_key_such_as_sales: The authorization key, such as `sales.customer.edit`. Patterns use `*` for any text and `?` for one character; backslash escapes literal punctuation.
texts.auth.the_single_object_identifier_or_val: The single object identifier or value being authorized.
texts.auth.comma_separated_values_inclusive_ra: Comma-separated values, inclusive ranges, `*`/`?` patterns and `!` exclusions. Enable Comparisons to use `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`; `!>`, `!>=`, `!<`, `!<=` then mean `<=`, `<`, `>=`, `>` and grant on their own. Numeric endpoints compare exact decimals; other endpoints compare case-sensitive text. Example with Comparisons enabled: `>=7000,!8000-8200`. Escape leading comparison punctuation for literals in that mode. With Comparisons off, `<` and `>` keep their literal meaning.
texts.auth.values_for_the_attributes_reference: Values for the attributes referenced by the assigned role and the roles it includes, for example `dlis.einvoice.channel` = `SK,CZ`.
texts.auth.interpret_leading_and_as_comparison: Interpret leading `<`, `>`, `!<` and `!>` as comparison operators. Existing entries keep this off until explicitly changed.
texts.auth.what_this_role_or_authorization_act: What this role or authorization action is for.
texts.auth.the_package_that_declares_this_role: The package that declares this role. Only its declaration changes the role; copy it to make your own version.
texts.auth.the_package_commit_whose_declaratio: The package commit whose declaration the role matches.
texts.auth.no_longer_declared_by_its_package_k: No longer declared by its package; kept while users or roles still use it.
texts.auth.why_no_reachable_role_granted_acces: Why no reachable role granted access.
texts.auth.evaluation_evidence_limited_to_the_: Evaluation evidence, limited to the first 100 entries.
texts.auth.the_first_reachable_role_whose_entr: The first reachable role whose entry allowed the check.
texts.screens.comma_separated_values_inclusive: Comma-separated values, inclusive ranges, `*`/`?` patterns and `!` exclusions; `*` allows every value. Comparisons `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` work directly. Double-quote literal text such as `"25-12-2026"` or `"a,b"`.
